title: Fuzzy reconciler: improve invoice line attribution for ambiguous rate-limit & proration events
creator: Maria Chen
description: Problem: We intermittently observe Stripe invoice adjustments or NetSuite mismatches where the raw meter events (rate-limit credits, subminute prorations, late usage) cannot be deterministically mapped to exported invoice lines. Root causes include retries that alter timestamps, near-boundary DST/tenant-timezone plan swaps, and concurrent quota overrides. Existing reconciler heuristics drop or create duplicate lines for ~0.6% of midcycle adjustments, leading to customer-facing negative adjustments and manual investigation work.
goals: 1) Build a reconciliation harness that uses fuzzy-match heuristics (time-window overlap, tokenized reason similarity, amount-signature, and tenant-bucket lineage) to increase automatic attribution coverage from ~98.6% to >=99.8% for ambiguous adjustments. 2) Provide a non-destructive dry-run mode that emits an explainable match score and decision trace for each ambiguous export line. 3) Implement a controlled backfill/repair runner for historic windows with a strict safety net (idempotency keys + human approval).
background: We already have deterministic matching for well-anchored usage windows. The remaining failures are skewed by clock jitter, webhook retry jitter, and mid-cycle plan switches that move the expected invoice anchor by minutes. Past fixes (timestamp-watermarking, anchor hysteresis) reduced volume but did not eliminate ambiguous attribution where multiple candidate usage deltas sum to the exported adjustment. Ops currently triages these with adhoc SQL and manual NetSuite edits; this is time-consuming and error-prone.
approach: - Prototype a fuzzy reconciliation algorithm that computes candidate matches with a composite score: time_distance_weighted, amount_similarity_ratio, reason_token_overlap (normalized), and lineage_continuity_score. - Expose a confidence threshold and triage buckets: AUTO_APPLY (score >= 0.95), REVIEW_QUEUE (0.70 <= score < 0.95), NO_MATCH (score < 0.70). - Add per-tenant heuristics toggle: for tenants with reserved capacity or invoice commit policies, require higher thresholds. - Implement dry-run comparator that runs alongside existing reconciler for 14 days and generates monitoring metrics (match_rate_by_bucket, false_positive_samples). - Backfill strategy: run only on invoices flagged as 'ambiguous=true' between 2025-07-01 and 2025-08-31; generate proposed export patches and require human sign-off via PR workflow before applying to production export manifest.
tradeoffs: - Fuzzy logic risks false positives that could modify exported invoice lines; mitigated via a conservative default threshold and human approval for changes. - Additional compute cost for heuristics and dry-run datasets; will be limited to nightly batch windows and sampled tenants. - Complexity increases test surface; invest in comprehensive property-based tests and a replay harness.
metrics:
- target_auto_resolution_rate: ">= 85% of ambiguous cases auto-applied"
- target_overall_reconciliation_accuracy: ">= 99.8%"
- false_positive_rate_in_review: "<= 0.5%"
- mean_time_to_triage_reduction: "from 6h to <= 1h for cases routed to review queue"
monitoring: New dashboards and alerts: billing.fuzzy_reconciler.match_rate, billing.fuzzy_reconciler.review_queue_size, billing.fuzzy_reconciler.false_positive_sampling_rate. Wire alerts to #billing-ops for REVIEW_QUEUE growth > 100/day and to oncall if AUTO_APPLY rollback triggers > 3 in 24h.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Dry-run produces match suggestions for >= 95% of historical ambiguous records in the sample window without altering exports. 2) Automated unit/property tests cover edge cases: plan swap at DST boundary, webhook retry reordering, multi-currency rounding. 3) Performance: reconciler dry-run completes nightly sample within 3 hours for 10k ambiguous events. 4) Runbook and rollback documented; human approval flow implemented in the console for backfill patches.
implementation_steps: 1) Design heuristic proto and ranking function (PRD link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILLING/Fuzzy+Reconciler+PRD). 2) Implement matching library and deterministic tie-breakers. 3) Integrate dry-run mode into export-postprocess pipeline behind feature flag. 4) Add telemetry and sampling endpoints. 5) Iterate thresholds on canary tenants. 6) Build backfill GUI for approvals and run controlled repair on a single tenant. 7) Gradually expand to wider tenant cohorts after sign-off.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: accidental invoice mutation -> Mitigation: dry-run + manual approval + immutable export manifest snapshotting. - Risk: algorithmic bias for certain tenant patterns -> Mitigation: per-tenant threshold overrides and monitoring-by-tenant. - Risk: missed regulatory/audit trace -> Mitigation: store full decision trace (explainability) and attach to export manifest; do not delete original lines, only append corrective entries with references.
